effectiveContext.name: Context Health implementation audit
effectiveContext.selectionRule: Files explicitly required by AGENTS.md for a significant Astro UI implementation: repository authority, routed workflow and quality documentation, and the mandatory implementation/UI skills.

overallSummary: The audited repository context has strong authority and task routing, and it covers the work needed for a static Astro UI change. Its main weaknesses are avoidable breadth in skills required for every implementation, indirect discovery for a few workflows, and repeated command summaries that require manual synchronization.
strengths: AGENTS.md explicitly distinguishes coding-agent authority from human-facing documentation and names source-of-truth files.
Change-type routing and task-specific skills make most architecture, UI, accessibility, and validation guidance discoverable.
The implementation guidance consistently favors static Astro output, semantic HTML, minimal JavaScript, and proportionate validation.

priorities.finding: Every implementation task is told to consult the full performance skill, even when the change does not affect dependencies, scripts, media, or interactive UI.
priorities.recommendation: Keep the safe-change and Astro skills mandatory, but route the performance skill only for the change types listed in its own trigger scope.

priorities.finding: The contact-worker route points to a directory with no local README, while the actual workflow is in deployment documentation.
priorities.recommendation: Add a small contact-worker README that links to the canonical deployment sections, then route AGENTS.md to that entry point.

priorities.finding: Command summaries are repeated in AGENTS.md, README.md, and docs/testing.md even though package.json is authoritative.
priorities.recommendation: Add a lightweight consistency check or generate the summaries from package.json so audience-specific copies cannot drift.

metrics.label: Context Precision
metrics.interpretation: Most loaded guidance is directly useful for this work, with some breadth and repetition that are not necessary for every implementation.

checks.label: Change types route to focused documentation
checks.interpretation: The routing table limits most documentation loading to the kind of change being made.

evidence.observation: The table maps content, architecture, styling, schema, deployment, contact-worker, and workflow changes to different references.

checks.label: Static UI guidance is scoped to the requested implementation
checks.interpretation: The Astro, accessibility, and CSS skills all provide directly applicable constraints for this report page.

evidence.observation: The selected skills separately cover static rendering, native semantics, focus and contrast, and token-based styles.

checks.label: Always-required skills stay narrow for all implementation tasks
checks.interpretation: The full performance playbook is relevant here but would add substantial unrelated context to many small implementation changes.

evidence.observation: AGENTS.md requires three skills for every implementation; the performance skill also covers dependencies, media, fonts, third-party resources, analytics, and animation.

checks.label: Repeated command summaries avoid redundant context
checks.interpretation: The copies serve different audiences, but loading more than one repeats information without adding much task value.

evidence.observation: Three files contain overlapping command lists for typecheck, lint, build, Lighthouse, and related checks.

metrics.label: Context Recall
metrics.interpretation: Major guidance is reachable, but specifications and contact-worker operations require an extra discovery step.

checks.label: Major change areas are routed from the authority file
checks.interpretation: The authority file exposes the principal documentation entry points needed for repository changes.

evidence.observation: AGENTS.md directly lists references for seven change areas and includes separate validation routing.

checks.label: Feature specifications are directly discoverable
checks.interpretation: Specifications are covered, but only after following the workflow-document route.

evidence.observation: AGENTS.md routes agent workflow generally; docs/agent-workflow.md then instructs agents to check specs.

checks.label: Contact-worker operations have a direct local entry point
checks.interpretation: The worker is named in routing, but the target directory does not explain where its operational workflow lives.

evidence.observation: AGENTS.md points contact-worker changes to contact-worker/, while deployment commands and secrets are documented under Deployment and Operations.

checks.label: Design-system guidance is discoverable
checks.interpretation: Architecture documentation names both the inventory and the agent guide as entry points.

evidence.observation: The sources-of-truth table links reusable components, shared styles, and design-system inventory to their canonical files.

checks.label: Task-specific skills are exposed by change type
checks.interpretation: The authority file distinguishes baseline implementation, UI, search, and metadata skill sets.

evidence.observation: AGENTS.md groups required skills under implementation, UI, search, and metadata/content route headings.

metrics.label: Sufficiency
metrics.interpretation: The selected context supports implementation and review end to end; contact-worker guidance is the clearest local documentation gap.

checks.label: Architecture and static-rendering constraints are documented
checks.interpretation: The context explains the page, component, style, script, and generated-output boundaries.

evidence.observation: Architecture lists the core source areas and generated directories; the Astro skill requires static output and minimal client JavaScript.

checks.label: Validation and browser-test workflows are documented
checks.interpretation: The context identifies the relevant type, lint, build, Lighthouse, and Playwright checks.

evidence.observation: Testing documentation describes available checks, when to run them, and how Playwright serves production output.

checks.label: Accessibility and contrast review have actionable guidance
checks.interpretation: Semantic controls, keyboard behavior, visible focus, contrast, and automated/manual verification are all addressed.

evidence.observation: The accessibility skill specifies native semantics, focus checks, color contrast, keyboard verification, and automated checks.

checks.label: Performance and asset-isolation review are covered
checks.interpretation: The performance skill provides the checks needed to prove page-specific CSS and zero feature JavaScript.

evidence.observation: The skill requires static rendering, page-scoped scripts, production bundle checks, and mobile verification.

checks.label: Review scope and stop conditions are explicit
checks.interpretation: The workflow can distinguish required fixes from scope expansion and unrelated changes.

evidence.observation: The safe-change skill defines boundaries and stop conditions, while the reviewer checklist defines request-fit criteria.

checks.label: Contact-worker changes are documented beside the worker source
checks.interpretation: Operational guidance is sufficient once found, but the worker directory itself lacks a documentation entry point.

evidence.observation: Deployment documentation covers local development, type checking, deploys, secrets, request flow, and rollback for the worker.

metrics.label: Authority Clarity
metrics.interpretation: Authority is explicit for agent behavior, exact commands, and design-system sources; duplicated command summaries still create synchronization risk.

checks.label: Agent instructions and human documentation have explicit roles
checks.interpretation: The repository clearly names AGENTS.md as coding-agent authority and source files as exact behavior.

evidence.observation: Documentation boundaries and authority are stated in two dedicated sections at the top of AGENTS.md.

checks.label: Exact package commands have a named source of truth
checks.interpretation: Readers can resolve command-summary differences against package.json.

evidence.observation: The authority table assigns exact scripts, schemas, routes, and behavior to package.json, source, and configuration files.

checks.label: Protected-file authority is explicit
checks.interpretation: The repository identifies files whose edits require explicit approval.

evidence.observation: AGENTS.md lists protected root configuration and documentation files and states the stop condition.

checks.label: Command guidance has no synchronization ambiguity
checks.interpretation: Authority is resolvable, but three manually maintained summaries can drift before a reader checks package.json.

evidence.observation: AGENTS.md, README.md, and testing documentation each maintain a command list with different coverage.

checks.label: Design-system sources of truth are explicit
checks.interpretation: The context distinguishes implementation files, inventory, and human guidance.

evidence.observation: Architecture maps reusable components, shared styles, and the inventory to separate canonical files.

metrics.label: Active Context Size
metrics.interpretation: The declared effective context contains 46,269 characters (~11,568 estimated tokens).

details.estimationMethod: Estimated tokens = ceil(characters / 4). This is an approximation, not a tokenizer result.

methodology.scoreCalculation: For each agent-assessed metric, contribution = check weight × result score. Weights total 1. The displayed score is the sum of contributions. Status thresholds are healthy at 85% or higher, needs attention at 70–84.9%, and at risk below 70%.
methodology.assessmentBoundary: Check result, impact classification, interpretation, and evidence observations are agent-assessed. pnpm context:health deterministically derives contributions, metric scores, score statuses, file character counts, token estimates, size status, and the size interpretation.

tokenEstimation.note: This approximation is not a tokenizer result.

methodology.activeContextThresholds: Healthy at 24,000 estimated tokens or fewer, needs attention from 24,001 through 48,000, and at risk above 48,000. These are review bands for this report, not model context-window limits.

limitations: Semantic findings are an agent assessment of repository guidance, not a measurement of model behavior or output quality.
The declared effective-context set is specific to this significant Astro UI audit; other tasks load different routed files and skills.
The four-characters-per-token estimate is deliberately simple and can differ materially from a real tokenizer.
The repository revision identifies the audited baseline commit. It does not claim to identify the later commit that contains this report.
